Ross borrowed some money from a bank, agreeing to pay the money back at a constant rate per month.
The table below shows the amount of money $L$ that's outstanding on the loan $n$ months since he started paying it back.
How much did Ross borrow?

| $n$ (months) | $10$ | $15$ | $20$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| $L$ (dollars) | $4000$ | $3000$ | $2000$ |

You may assume that the relationship between $n$ and $L$ is linear.

> A calculator is required to answer this question.

Mark delivers packages to houses. The table below shows the number of packages $P$ remaining for Mark to deliver $n$ hours after he started working.
How many packages did Mark start with?

| $n$ (hours) | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| $P$ (packages) | $64$ | $34$ | $4$ |

You may assume that the relationship between $n$ and $P$ is linear.

> A calculator is required to answer this question.

Stephanie is a geologist who began studying land subsidence due to a geological fault. The table below shows the land subsidence  $C,$ in centimeters, $n$ weeks after the study began. How many centimeters of subsidence were there at the beginning of the study?

| $n$ (weeks) | $10$ | $15$ | $20$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $C$ (centimeters) | $11$ | $13.5$ | $16$ |

You may assume that the relationship between $n$ and $C$ is linear.
